title: Local and global finite Tor dimension on a quasi-compact pro-étale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-compact scheme, meaning that every open cover of its underlying space has a finite subcover [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $A$ be a commutative ring. Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ with its pro-étale topology [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the constant ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(A_X))$, the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a site object $U$, write $M|_U$ for derived restriction to the slice ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{proét}}/U,A_X|_U)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction, def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Derived tensor and its cohomology use [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. The following are equivalent:

1. There are integers $a\leq b$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X$-module sheaf $N$, one has $H^q(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$.
2. For every site object $U$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ and integers $a_i\leq b_i$ such that, for every degree-zero $A_X|_{U_i}$-module sheaf $N_i$ on the slice site, one has $H^q(M|_{U_i}\otimes^L_{A_X|_{U_i}}N_i)=0$ for $q\notin[a_i,b_i]$.

No boundedness, constructibility, Noetherian, or completeness hypothesis is imposed on $M$, $A$, or $X$ beyond quasi-compactness of $X$.

source.place: Tag 09C2, lemma-describe-constructible-complexes, proof: making local finite Tor dimension uniform on quasi-compact X; the local-to-global argument applies to arbitrary constant coefficient module complexes. Local finite Tor dimension is Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, in sites-cohomology.tex.

proof.text:
First record the restriction calculation needed below. For a site object $V$, the localization morphism $j_V$ has coefficient map the identity on $A_X|_V$, so its module pullback is exactly restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. This functor is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]; hence its derived pullback is termwise restriction, the functor of [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to this ringed localization and the objects $M,N[0]$, where $N$ is an arbitrary global module sheaf. It gives $(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)|_V\simeq M|_V\otimes^L_{A_X|_V}N|_V$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to the same exact restriction gives
$$H^q(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)|_V\cong H^q(M|_V\otimes^L_{A_X|_V}N|_V).$$
The tensor comparison is for arbitrary unbounded derived objects and arbitrary ring sheaves; the cohomology comparison is for every integer $q$. Thus neither comparison requires constructibility or boundedness.

source.place: Tag 07A4, lemma-pullback-tensor-product, specialized to the localization morphism of Modules on Sites Tag 04IX (definition-localize-ringed-site); exact restriction and its degreewise cohomology comparison.

proof.text: Assume (1), with interval $[a,b]$. For every site object $U$, apply [lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction] with $\mathcal O=A_X$ and $E=M$. It gives the same Tor interval for $M|_U$, tested against every module sheaf on the slice, including those not obtained by restricting a global module. The singleton identity covering $\{U\xrightarrow{1}U\}$ therefore satisfies (2). Identity families are coverings by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. The restriction $E|_U$ of the cited theorem is [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction], termwise restriction of a chosen representative followed by $Q_U$; the restriction $M|_U$ of the statement is [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction], the functor induced on derived categories by the same exact termwise restriction. Both send $Q(C)$ to an object isomorphic to $Q_U(C|_U)$ for every complex $C$, so $M|_U$ and the cited $E|_U$ are isomorphic. Likewise the derived tensor of [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude], formed from any K-flat resolution, agrees up to isomorphism with the K-flat flat-term model of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], since a K-flat flat-term resolution is in particular K-flat. Vanishing of cohomology sheaves is invariant under isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08H5, lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback, specialized to ringed localization; Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude.

proof.text: Assume (2). A scheme is covered by affine open subschemes [def-pc-scheme], and quasi-compactness [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] selects a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{\alpha=1}^t W_\alpha$. These are site objects, and this Zariski cover is a pro-étale cover by [sk-def-pe-site]. For each $W_\alpha$, apply (2) to obtain a covering $\{Z_{\alpha i}\to W_\alpha\}_i$ and intervals $[a_{\alpha i},b_{\alpha i}]$ for the restrictions of $M$. By the affine-target clause of [sk-def-pe-site], this covering refines to a finite affine covering $\{V_{\alpha j}\to W_\alpha\}_{j=1}^{m_\alpha}$, each map factoring through some $Z_{\alpha,i(\alpha,j)}$. Composing these coverings with $\{W_\alpha\to X\}$ gives a finite covering $\{V_{\alpha j}\to X\}$ by the composition axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. All objects and covers are taken in the chosen small site, up to its skeleton equivalences. No quasi-separatedness of $X$ is needed: finite refinement is used separately over each affine target.

source.place: Tag 0989, definition-fpqc-covering; affine-target finite refinement as stated by sk-def-pe-site; Tag 098B, lemma-etale-proetale; Tag 098C, lemma-proetale, composition of covering families.

proof.text:
For each selected pair $(\alpha,j)$, restrict the Tor interval on $Z_{\alpha,i(\alpha,j)}$ further to $V_{\alpha j}$ using [lem-sf-site-tor-interval-restriction], now on the ringed site $X_{\mathrm{proét}}/Z_{\alpha,i(\alpha,j)}$. The relocalization identity in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] identifies this twice restricted object with $M|_{V_{\alpha j}}$ and its coefficient ring with $A_X|_{V_{\alpha j}}$. Thus its Tor amplitude lies in $[a_{\alpha,i(\alpha,j)},b_{\alpha,i(\alpha,j)}]$, with arbitrary slice modules as tests. Define
$$a=\min\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{a_{\alpha,i(\alpha,j)}\}_{\alpha,j}\bigr),\qquad b=\max\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{b_{\alpha,i(\alpha,j)}\}_{\alpha,j}\bigr).$$
These are finite nonempty sets of integers. Then $a\leq0\leq b$, and every selected local Tor interval is contained in $[a,b]$. The inserted zero also handles the empty cover of the empty scheme. The identification of the cited derived restriction and tensor with those of the statement is the one made in step 2.

source.place: Tag 08H5, lemma-tor-amplitude-pullback; relocalization is Sites Tag 03EH, lemma-relocalize.

proof.text: Let $N$ be any degree-zero global $A_X$-module sheaf, and let $q\notin[a,b]$. Put $F=H^q(M\otimes^L_{A_X}N)$. Step 1 identifies $F|_{V_{\alpha j}}$ with $H^q(M|_{V_{\alpha j}}\otimes^L N|_{V_{\alpha j}})$. The latter vanishes by step 4: $N|_{V_{\alpha j}}$ is an allowed slice module and $q$ lies outside its selected local interval. Consequently $F$ restricts to zero on every member of the finite covering of step 3. This implication uses only the displayed restriction calculation and the defining vanishing condition, with no extension or descent of slice test modules required.

source.place: Tag 08FZ, definition-tor-amplitude, applied after the explicit comparison of step 1.

proof.text: To conclude $F=0$, take any site object $T$. Base change of the covering from step 3 gives a covering $\{T\times_X V_{\alpha j}\to T\}$. By the sectionwise rule for localized sheaves [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], $F(T\times_X V_{\alpha j})=0$ since each such object maps to $V_{\alpha j}$. The sheaf equalizer axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] makes $F(T)\to\prod_{\alpha,j}F(T\times_X V_{\alpha j})$ injective; its target is the zero group, hence $F(T)=0$. This holds for all $T$, so $F=0$. When $X$ is empty, the same argument uses the empty covering and its empty product, the zero group. Since $N$ and $q\notin[a,b]$ were arbitrary, (1) follows, completing the equivalence.

split_report.summary: Preserved the arbitrary constant-coefficient statement. Proved both implications using the existing ringed-site Tor restriction theorem, exact restriction and derived tensor comparison. Uniformized bounds on finite affine refinements and proved global vanishing directly from the sheaf axiom, including the empty scheme. No new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes det-lem-integral-models-stacks, proof step identifying locally finite Tor dimension of the first residue reduction with a single global Tor interval, expanding the uniformity sentence of Stacks 09C2 on the integral-models route.

tool_uses.why: Its arbitrary-ringed-topos tensor comparison specializes to localization; the integral-models unit does not supply this general tensor identity.
Its arbitrary-ringed-site statement preserves a fixed interval against every slice module, for both global-to-local and refinement; the unit gives no such general restriction theorem.
The pro-etale topology, including finite affine refinement for affine targets and Zariski covers, supplies the covering facts used to uniformize bounds without a Noetherian hypothesis.

Its K-flat flat-term model of the ringed-site derived tensor identifies the tensor of the cited Tor restriction theorem with the Tor-amplitude tensor of the statement; the integral-models unit gives no tensor convention of its own.
